choice: Restricted attachment list/detail reads to users with view permission on the attached model's type, because any authenticated user could previously read all attachments regardless of their permissions.
final:
I fixed a read-access hole in the attachment API: any logged-in user could list or fetch every attachment, whatever their permissions on the part, order, stock item or other object it belonged to. The requested test command passes (53 tests, OK).

Writes were already checked per model, but reads only required a login. A user with no roles could therefore list attachments and get their file URLs and comments for any model. That includes models like purchase orders and company records that they couldn't otherwise see.

The change is in `AttachmentMixin.get_queryset` in `common/api.py`. For GET requests, it now limits results to attachments whose model type the user can view. It checks the same two things the serializer already checks on writes, the user's role and the model's `check_related_permission`. Superusers see everything. An attachment you can't view now returns 404 on the detail endpoint, and it no longer appears in list results.

I left write requests unfiltered. The existing edit/delete checks still run and still return 403, and an existing test depends on that.

I added `test_view_permission` to `common/test_api.py`. It checks that a user with no roles sees an empty list and gets 404 on a detail request. With `part.view` only, they see part attachments and get 404 on a stock-location attachment. I dropped a final step that granted a second role mid-test. It failed, and I suspect the test client reuses one user object with stale permissions, but I didn't confirm that.

CHOICE: Restricted attachment list/detail reads to users with view permission on the attached model's type, because any authenticated user could previously read all attachments regardless of their permissions.
